clue.text: Stock controller's pen

parts.note: reads like a ballpoint used by a stores clerk, but stock here is livestock and the pen an enclosure that holds them

explanation.surface: A warehouse manager's ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A corral is an enclosure where cattle or horses are kept in, the pen that controls livestock.

clue.text: Eton chap seen around in Whitehall

indicators.note: around tells us the letters of the words Eton chap are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A public schoolboy is spotted in the government district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall is the London street of government offices, home of the national war memorial; 'seen' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The national war memorial stands in the middle of the London street of government offices.

clue.text: Does it provide treatment for the hot and peevish?

parts.note: something red-hot glows red
peevish means irritable, cross

explanation.surface: Is there medical help for someone flushed and grumpy?
explanation.definitionFit: The international humanitarian organisation gives first aid and medical care.

clue.text: A point we raised once more

parts.note: N, north, is a compass point

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word we is written upwards, back to front

explanation.surface: A remark about lifting a sharp tip again.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something afresh means doing it a second time.

clue.text: Partisan assembly produces a candidate

indicators.note: assembly suggests putting the letters of Partisan together again in a different order

explanation.surface: A gathering of party loyalists picks someone to stand for election.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone seeking office or a position is an aspiring hopeful.

clue.text: Demonstrate concern in the entertainment industry

parts.note: to demonstrate is to show
a concern is a firm, a business

explanation.surface: Showing worry about the world of film and theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre, film and music together are known as the world of showbiz.

clue.text: Piece of news I encountered on return

indicators.note: on return tells us the letters of I and met are read back to front, upwards in this down clue

parts.note: encountered means met

explanation.surface: A news story someone came across on getting home.
explanation.definitionFit: A single report or article in a bulletin is called an item.

clue.text: A student with many grants

parts.note: L is a learner, a student driver
lots means many

explanation.surface: One undergraduate receives lots of funding awards.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to assign or give out shares, so grants is a synonym.

clue.text: Check an oarsman's support

definitions.meaning: to check a plan is to frustrate or foil it
the crosswise seat in a rowing boat on which the rower sits

explanation.definitionFit: To foil is to block someone, and a rowing boat's cross-bench seat carries the same name.

clue.text: Agreed with the head

parts.note: reads as siding with the boss, but means showing assent by a movement of one's head

explanation.surface: Sided with the headmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip of the head is the gesture of assent, so giving it means agreeing.

clue.text: Firm rule about the French salad

indicators.note: about says the firm and the rule go around the French article

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a law is a rule
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: A company regulation on French-style salads.
explanation.definitionFit: Shredded cabbage in mayonnaise is a familiar side salad.

clue.text: Wait to start a game of ping-pong?

definitions.meaning: to wait is to serve meals to diners as a waiter

definitions.text: to start a game of ping-pong?
definitions.meaning: table tennis opens with a serve over the table

explanation.definitionFit: A waiter brings dishes to diners, and table tennis opens with a serve; the question mark flags the playful second sense.

clue.text: Cutting pastry

definitions.meaning: a cutting remark is sharp or sarcastic
a pastry case with a sweet filling

explanation.definitionFit: A sharp remark is tart, and a fruit pie in a crust is a tart too.

clue.text: Vivid colour brought back by a classic event

indicators.note: brought back means the letters of red are reversed

parts.note: red is a vivid colour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brilliant hue returns thanks to a traditional occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The English Classics are five major flat horse races; the Derby at Epsom is the most famous.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epsom horse race is one of the five Classics of British flat racing.

clue.text: Move with a little spooning

definitions.meaning: turning a spoon in a cup to mix it

explanation.definitionFit: To rouse is to move, and mixing tea with a spoon is the same word.

clue.text: Wrest apart and scatter

indicators.note: apart suggests the letters of Wrest are pulled to pieces and rearranged

explanation.surface: Tear something apart and fling it about.
explanation.definitionFit: To strew is to spread things loosely over a surface, as you would scatter them.

clue.text: Turkish leader elected for a second time

parts.note: an aga is an Ottoman commander or chief
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: A Turkish chief wins office once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Once more, repeated, is what the adverb means.

clue.text: Encouraging omen is a plus to any mathematician

definitions.meaning: a hopeful indication of good things

explanation.definitionFit: A hopeful indication is called this, and so is the plus symbol in arithmetic.

clue.text: One flies from such crimes

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is made out of the letters of One flies, reworked

explanation.surface: A criminal escapes the scene after serious offences.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a fugitive; 'from' is the anagram signal, rearranging the eight letters of ONE FLIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Serious offences such as murder or burglary are classed as felonies.

clue.text: Vessels pilots take in the morning

indicators.note: take in says the verb pilots surrounds the morning abbreviation

parts.note: a pilot steers a ship
AM, ante meridiem, is the morning

explanation.surface: Ships' pilots board early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships driven by steam engines are vessels.

clue.text: Keep quiet and enlist marine detachment

indicators.note: detachment hints that the letters of enlist marine break up and form something new

explanation.surface: Say nothing and sign up for a unit of marines.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold one's tongue is to say nothing.

clue.text: Extra large fender

definitions.meaning: the American word for a car ... is fender

explanation.definitionFit: A bumper harvest is huge, and a car's protective bar has the same name.

clue.text: Did not see, but heard, the spray

indicators.note: heard says the word for a fine spray is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a fine spray of water droplets is mist

explanation.surface: Someone failed to spot the drizzle but could hear it.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail to notice something is to overlook it.

clue.text: One the soldier returns to after leave

definitions.text: the soldier returns to after leave
definitions.meaning: the military group a soldier belongs to

explanation.definitionFit: A single item counts as one, and a soldier rejoins their regiment or battalion after time off.

clue.text: Good man gets a warning to say nothing and hide away

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man
sh is the hushing warning to keep quiet

explanation.surface: A virtuous man is told to keep quiet and lie low.
explanation.definitionFit: To stash something is to store it secretly.

clue.text: Concluding passage in flamenco dancing

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words flamenco dancing, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: The final section of a flamenco performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took only 'Concluding' as the definition; the answer is a noun, so 'Concluding passage' defines it and 'in' alone signals the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing section of a piece of music is its coda.

clue.text: In this place he really is friendless

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: is friendless says the word for a friend, ally, is taken out of really

explanation.surface: A lonely man in this town has no friends at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friendless' asks for ALLY, a friend, to be removed from REALLY, leaving RE.
explanation.definitionFit: This adverb means at the present spot.

clue.text: French priest one may go to Lourdes to find

definitions.meaning: a parish priest in France, the title used for a vicar there

definitions.text: one may go to Lourdes to find
definitions.meaning: Lourdes is a French pilgrimage town famous for healing

explanation.definitionFit: A curé is a French parish priest, and pilgrims visit the Lourdes shrine hoping to be healed.

clue.text: Non-stop walker

parts.note: reads as a tireless hiker, but means a pedestrian who goes past without stopping

explanation.surface: A tireless hiker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone strolling past without halting is a pedestrian going by.

clue.text: Raised in company of wolves

indicators.note: in says the word for raised goes inside the company

parts.note: a shipping line is a company
raised means up

explanation.surface: Brought up among a wolf pack, like a feral child.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective from the Latin lupus describes anything wolfish.

clue.text: Was a shade embarrassed?

parts.note: reads as being slightly awkward, but a shade is a colour tint, and an embarrassed face blushes

explanation.surface: Was someone slightly ashamed?
explanation.definitionFit: Going crimson in the face is the visible sign of blushing with embarrassment.

clue.text: Is against using Latin

parts.note: reads as objecting to a classical language, but means the Latin word for against

explanation.surface: Someone objects to teaching Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin preposition meaning opposite or against is used in legal case names and sports fixtures.
